recovery_balance.meaning: HRV z-score minus load z-score; below 0 = load outpacing recovery

aerobic_decoupling_pct.note: first-half vs second-half efficiency drift; under 5% = aerobically sound

drivers: HRV is elevated (+7.9 ms vs baseline, +12.0%), indicating parasympathetic resilience
Sleep duration improved (+0.5 h/night vs baseline) but remains chronically low (14/14 nights <7h)
Resting HR declined (-1.9 bpm), supporting recovery
Training readiness score (45) is below 7-day avg (53.8) and Garmin status is RECOVERY_1
ACWR = 0.7 — in the low/detraining range, reflecting reduced acute load relative to chronic
Recovery balance = 1.17 (above 0), meaning HRV z-score currently exceeds load z-score
readiness.guidance: The athlete is not acutely fatigued but is operating on a narrow recovery margin due to persistent sleep debt; priority this week is reinforcing recovery capacity, not adding stress.

monthly_review.summary: This month shows reduced volume and slower average pace versus last month, with modest improvements in aerobic efficiency and cadence — consistent with a deliberate downshift into recovery-focused training.
monthly_review.highlight: Cadence increased by 32 spm from last month — the largest single-month jump in the 5-month history — and aligns with recent runs showing cadence consistently ≥148 spm, suggesting a successful neuromuscular adaptation to lower-impact, higher-cadence running.

goal_tracker.message: To match last month’s 82.4 km would require 34.1 km across 5 remaining sessions — an average of 6.8 km/session — but given compromised sleep continuity (14/14 nights <7h) and RECOVERY_1 status, chasing this volume is inadvisable and risks undermining aerobic gains and injury resilience.

insights.title: Chronic sleep debt correlates with elevated Running Economy values
insights.body: Despite HRV and resting HR improving, Running Economy median remains at 253.5 ml O2/kg/km (‘Recreational’ rating) — well above the sub-200 threshold for trained runners — and coincides with 100% of last 14 nights under 7 hours sleep; research shows <6.5h sleep impairs mitochondrial efficiency and increases oxygen cost at submaximal intensities.

insights.title: Low ACWR (0.7) reflects intentional load reduction, not stagnation
insights.body: ACWR dropped from 1.0+ implied by last month’s 638 TRIMP (June) and 526 (July) to 0.7 this month — matching the 29% drop in weekly TRIMP (449.8 vs 491.2 baseline) and aligning with the shift toward Z1/Z2 dominance (65% of run time this month vs 48% last month), confirming a deliberate recovery phase.

insights.title: Cadence surge improves stride efficiency without increasing vertical oscillation
insights.body: Cadence rose from 118 spm (July) to 150 spm (August) while vertical oscillation stayed stable (6.6–8.0 mm) and ground contact time decreased (309 → 299 ms avg); this suggests improved neuromuscular coordination rather than compensatory bouncing — supported by aerobic decoupling improving to 4.8% (under 5% threshold) on the 12 km long run.

insights.title: Decoupling variability signals intermittent fatigue management issues
insights.body: Recent decoupling values swing widely (0.84% to 9.37%), with median 7.11% — above the 5% target — and the worst value (9.37%) occurring during July’s highest-volume week (638 TRIMP); this implies that when load temporarily spikes, aerobic stability erodes before full recovery resets it.

recommendations.action: Zone 1–2 easy run, HR ≤132 bpm, 5.0 km on Tuesday — no pace target, focus on cadence ≥152 spm and relaxed breathing
recommendations.reason: Supports aerobic base maintenance while honoring current RECOVERY_1 status and low ACWR; cadence target leverages recent neuromuscular gains without cardiac or metabolic strain.

recommendations.action: 10-minute post-run mobility routine (hip flexor + calf + tibialis anterior focus) after every run, tracked via Garmin Body Battery ‘recovery time’ estimate
recommendations.reason: Ground contact time remains elevated (298–385 ms) and vertical oscillation increased slightly (6.6→8.0 mm), suggesting residual stiffness — especially notable on the 8.0 km run where GC rose to 385 ms and HR dropped to 111 bpm (likely compensatory fatigue).

recommendations.action: Sleep hygiene intervention: lights out by 22:30, no screens after 21:30, and 10-min guided breathwork (4-7-8) starting tonight — verified via Garmin sleep staging and HRV trends over next 3 days
recommendations.reason: 14/14 nights <7h sleep is the strongest modifiable limiter to Running Economy and decoupling stability; even 30 extra minutes of consolidated deep sleep can reduce oxygen cost by ~2–3% within 48h.

risk_flags.risk: Chronic sleep debt impairing aerobic efficiency and injury resilience
risk_flags.evidence: 14/14 nights <7h sleep in last 14 days; Running Economy stuck at 253.5 ml O2/kg/km (Recreational rating); vertical oscillation increased to 8.0 mm on longest recent runs
risk_flags.action: Prioritize sleep extension and consistency before increasing volume or intensity

risk_flags.risk: Inconsistent aerobic decoupling signaling latent fatigue
risk_flags.evidence: Median recent decoupling = 7.11%, exceeding 5% threshold; worst value (9.37%) occurred during high-load week (638 TRIMP in June); latest value (4.8%) recovered only after 2 weeks of reduced load
risk_flags.action: Delay introduction of Z4 intervals until decoupling median stabilizes ≤5% for 3 consecutive weeks

weekly_focus.description: Leverage strong HRV and cadence adaptation to reinforce efficient movement patterns — not increase load — while closing the sleep gap that’s constraining aerobic economy and durability.
suggested_sessions: Z1/Z2 easy run with cadence focus
Short mobility-integrated run (3–4 km, HR ≤130, cadence ≥152 spm)
Active recovery walk + breathwork (45 min, HR ≤110)
